verses.pali: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
verses.english: “Once upon a time, mendicants, as Sakka, lord of gods, was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

verses.pali: ‘yopi me assa supaccatthiko tassapāhaṁ na dubbheyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘I should never betray even a sworn enemy.’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkassa devānamindassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena sakko devānamindo tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: And then Vepacitti, lord of titans, knowing Sakka’s train of thought, approached him.

verses.pali: Addasā kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: Sakka saw Vepacitti coming off in the distance,

verses.pali: ‘Yadeva te, mārisa, pubbe cittaṁ, tadeva tvaṁ mā pajahāsī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Good fellow, don’t give up the idea you just had!’
‘Swear, Vepacitti, that you won’t betray me.’
‘Whatever bad things happen to a liar,
or to someone who slanders the noble ones,
or to someone who betrays a friend,
anyone who betrays you, Sujā’s husband.’”
